## Getting started

RapBooster sends WhatsApp messages to your customers from your own WhatsApp numbers, right from this computer. You link a number, add your contacts, write a message once, and RapBooster sends it to everyone at a safe, steady pace. It can also answer customers for you with automatic replies, chatbot menus and an AI assistant, while you follow every conversation in one Inbox.

A short checklist on the Dashboard walks you through the first steps. Each step ticks itself when it is done. You can hide it at any time and bring it back from Help Center.

### The getting-started checklist

1. **Link your WhatsApp number.** Scan a QR code from WhatsApp on your phone, like WhatsApp Web. ([Devices](#devices))
2. **Import contacts.** Add a list of customers from a file, a Google Sheet or your phone. ([Contacts](#contacts))
3. **Create a message template.** Write your message once. Use `{{Name}}` to greet each person by name. ([Templates](#templates))
4. **Send your first campaign.** Start with a small test list of your own numbers before you send to customers. ([Campaigns](#campaigns))
5. **Optional: set up auto-replies.** Answer common questions automatically with a keyword rule, a chatbot menu or the AI bot. ([Automation](#automation))

### Help while you work

- Press F1 on any screen, or click the "?" next to its title, to read about that screen and search all of the help.
- Small "?" icons next to settings explain what they do. Hover over them, or reach them with the Tab key.
- The first time you open a screen, RapBooster offers a short guided tour. You can restart any tour from Help Center.
- Help Center, in the Setup part of the sidebar, has everything in this guide.

### Guided tours

Tours are available for these screens: [Dashboard](#dashboard), [Devices](#devices), [Contacts](#contacts), [Templates](#templates), [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Inbox](#inbox), [Automation](#automation), [AI Bot](#ai-bot).

## Safety rules

WhatsApp bans numbers that behave like spammers, and a banned number cannot be recovered. RapBooster has safety limits switched on from the start. These rules keep your numbers safe.

### Only message people who want to hear from you

Messages to strangers get blocked and reported, and reports are what get numbers banned. Use lists of your own customers and people who gave you their number.

### Keep the daily cap on

Each phone sends at most 200 automated messages a day unless you change it in Settings › Sending & safety. When the cap is reached, sending waits until the next day. A cap of 0 means no limit, which is risky.

### Respect quiet hours

By default, campaigns, follow-up sequences, bulk group messages and warmup pause between 21:00 and 09:00, this computer's time, and carry on in the morning. Replies to customers (AI bot, chatbot flows, keyword, welcome and away replies) and messages you schedule for a set time still go out at any hour, within the daily limit.

### Warm up new numbers

A new number starts at 20 messages a day and grows over ten days. Switch on Warmup on the Devices screen for any number that is new or has not sent much before.

### Send slowly and vary your words

Keep the random delays and sleep pauses. Use spintax (`{Hi|Hello}`) and merge tags (`{{Name}}`) so no two messages are identical.

### Honour every opt-out

Anyone who replies STOP (or another opt-out word you choose) goes on the opt-out list. RapBooster never sends them campaigns, sequences or automatic replies. Only remove someone if they ask.

### Test with a small list first

Before any big campaign, send it to two or three of your own numbers. Check the wording, the merge tags and any buttons on a real phone.

### Stop when things go wrong

If many messages fail, or WhatsApp shows a warning on the phone, pause your campaigns at once. The health breaker pauses a phone by itself when failures look like a ban is coming.

## Dashboard

The Dashboard is your home screen. It shows how many contacts, connected phones, campaigns and templates you have, how many campaign messages went out today, and how each phone is doing against its daily limit. It also tells you when a customer is waiting for a person in the Inbox.

Find it: click **Dashboard** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Check how today is going

1. Click Dashboard at the top of the sidebar.
2. Look at "Sent today" and "Failed today". They count campaign messages since midnight.
3. Look at "Device usage today". Each bar shows how many messages a phone sent against its daily limit.
4. A "Warmup" label means the phone is new and its limit is still growing.
5. A "Paused for safety" label means RapBooster stopped that phone for a while. Open Devices to see why.

#### Find customers who are waiting for you

1. Look at the two cards under the daily numbers.
2. "Escalated chats" are conversations the bot handed to a person.
3. "AI drafts awaiting approval" are AI replies waiting for you to approve.
4. Click either card to open the Inbox and answer them.

#### Read the last 7 days chart

1. Find the "Last 7 days" panel.
2. Each day shows messages Sent, Failed, Delivered, Read and Replied.
3. Use the legend to see which colour is which.
4. A rising Failed line is a warning sign. Slow down and check your phones before sending more.

#### Use the getting-started checklist

1. After the welcome message, a "Getting started" list appears on the Dashboard.
2. Each step ticks itself when you finish it. You do not need to tick anything.
3. Click "Show me" next to a step. RapBooster opens the right screen and gives you a short tour.
4. Click "Hide checklist" when you no longer need it.
5. To bring it back, open Help Center and choose "Show the getting-started checklist again".

### Tips

- The numbers update by themselves while the Dashboard is open. You never need to refresh.
- "Running Campaigns" includes paused campaigns, because they still have messages left to send.
- "Active Devices" counts only phones that are connected right now.

### Be careful

- If "Failed today" keeps climbing, pause your campaigns and check the Devices screen before you send more. Many failures in a row can mean WhatsApp is limiting the number.

### Questions

#### Why does Active Devices show fewer phones than I linked?

It only counts phones that are connected at this moment. A phone that is switched off, offline or logged out is not counted. Open Devices to reconnect it.

#### Do inbox replies count in "Sent today"?

No. "Sent today" and "Failed today" count campaign messages only. Inbox replies, bot replies and sequence steps still count toward each phone's daily limit, which you see under "Device usage today".

#### The green safety notice disappeared. How do I see my limits again?

The notice shows once. Your daily limit and quiet hours are always in Settings, under "Sending & safety".

See also: [Inbox](#inbox), [Devices](#devices), [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety).

## Devices

A device is one WhatsApp number linked to RapBooster, the same way WhatsApp Web is linked to your phone. You can link up to 20 numbers. Each card shows whether the number is connected, how many messages it sent today against its daily limit, and its safety settings, such as warmup for new numbers.

Find it: click **Devices** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Link your WhatsApp number with a QR code

1. Click Devices in the sidebar, then "+ Add Device".
2. Type a Device Name you will recognise, such as "Shop phone".
3. Click "Generate QR & Connect". A QR code appears.
4. On your phone, open WhatsApp, then Settings, then "Linked Devices", then "Link a Device".
5. Point your phone at the QR code on the screen.
6. Wait a few seconds. The window closes and the card shows Connected.

#### Link with a pairing code instead

1. Click "+ Add Device", type a Device Name, and open the "Pairing code" tab.
2. Type the phone number with its country code, such as +91 98765 43210.
3. Click "Get pairing code". An 8-character code appears.
4. On your phone, open WhatsApp, then "Linked Devices", then "Link a Device", then "Link with phone number instead".
5. Type the code on your phone. The card shows Connected when it is done.

#### Warm up a new number

1. Find the card of the new number.
2. Switch on Warmup. The number starts at day 1.
3. Its daily limit starts at 20 messages and grows each day for ten days, up to your normal daily limit.
4. The caption shows the day and today's limit. Leave it on until it says "Ramp complete".

#### Fix a number that is not connected

1. Make sure the phone is switched on and has internet.
2. Click Reconnect on the card and wait a few seconds.
3. If the card says "Logged out", the link was removed from the phone. Link it again with "+ Add Device".
4. If a red message is shown on the card, read it. It says what went wrong.

#### Understand "Paused for safety"

1. When many messages fail in a row, RapBooster pauses that number to protect it. The card says why and when it resumes.
2. Check the phone: is WhatsApp showing a warning, or is the number restricted?
3. Slow down your campaigns before sending more.
4. Click "Resume now" only when you are sure the number is fine.

### Settings explained

- **Warmup**: For new numbers. Day 1 allows 20 messages, rising each day for ten days until your normal daily cap. Optional warmup conversations let your own numbers chat with each other.

### Tips

- Keep the phone charged and online. WhatsApp disconnects linked devices if the phone stays offline for about two weeks.
- The usage bar shows messages sent today against the daily limit. It resets at midnight.
- A "Business" badge means the number uses WhatsApp Business. Click Re-check if you change the account type.
- Logout unlinks the number from RapBooster. Use it before you give the phone away.

### Be careful

- New numbers get banned most easily. Switch on Warmup for any number that is less than a few weeks old, or has not sent many messages before.
- Never send many messages from a number that was just linked. Let it chat normally for a few days first.
- If WhatsApp shows a warning on the phone, stop all campaigns on that number straight away.

### Questions

#### The QR code does not scan. What can I try?

Make the window bigger and hold the phone steady about 20 cm away. The code changes every 20 seconds or so, which is normal. If it stops changing, close the window and click "+ Add Device" again, or use a pairing code.

#### Do I need to keep my phone near the computer?

No. After linking, the phone only needs to be switched on with internet now and then. It does not need to be near the computer.

#### Why is "+ Add Device" greyed out?

You have reached the limit of 20 devices.

See also: [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety), [Dashboard](#dashboard), [Campaigns](#campaigns), [WhatsApp Groups](#whatsapp-groups).

## Contacts

Contacts is where you keep the people you message, in lists such as "Customers" or "Leads". You can add people by hand, import a CSV, Excel or contact-card file or a Google Sheet, or copy the numbers your linked phones already know. You can also tag people, check which numbers are on WhatsApp, and manage the opt-out list of people who asked not to be messaged.

Find it: click **Contacts** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Create a contact list

1. Click Contacts in the sidebar, then "+ New List".
2. Type a List Name, such as "Customers".
3. Optionally type extra columns in "Custom Fields", separated by commas, such as Company, City.
4. Click "Create List". Name and Mobile are always included. Every custom field becomes a merge tag for templates.

#### Import contacts from a file

1. Open the list, then click Import.
2. On "From a file", click "Choose file…" and pick a CSV, Excel (.xlsx) or contact-card (.vcf) file. Click "Read file".
3. Check that each column points to the right field. One column must go to Mobile.
4. Answer "Do these numbers already include their country code?". If not, type your country code, such as +91.
5. Choose what happens when a number is already in the list, then click Import.
6. A message says how many were imported, skipped and invalid.

#### Import from a Google Sheet

1. In Google Sheets, click Share and set it to "Anyone with the link can view".
2. Copy the link of the tab you want.
3. In RapBooster, open the list, click Import, then choose "Google Sheets".
4. Paste the link and click "Read sheet". Then map the columns and import as with a file.

#### Import the numbers your phone already knows

1. Click "Import from WhatsApp".
2. Under "Who to import", choose Everyone, "Saved contacts" or "Chats (incl. unsaved numbers)". You can limit chats to the last few days.
3. Choose which phones to take numbers from, and look at the preview.
4. Type a name for the new list and click "Import into a new list".
5. A number known to several phones is imported once.

#### Tag contacts

1. Click "Manage tags" at the top. Type a tag name, such as VIP, pick a colour and click "Add tag".
2. In a list, tick the people you want to tag.
3. In the bar that appears, choose the tag and click "Tag selected".
4. Use the "All tags" filter to show only people with one tag. Campaigns and sequences can target tags.

#### Manage the opt-out list

1. Click the Opt-outs tab at the top of the Contacts screen.
2. To add numbers by hand, type them with their country code and click "Add to opt-outs".
3. To add many at once, import a CSV or TXT file of numbers.
4. Under "Automatic opt-outs", choose the words that opt someone out, such as STOP, and whether to send a confirmation.
5. Click Remove only if the person asked to receive messages again.

### Settings explained

- **When a number already exists in this list**: Skip keeps the contact you already have. Overwrite replaces it with the row from the file. A number can only be in a list once, so "Import anyway" still keeps the existing contact and adds every new number.
- **Country code**: If your numbers are written without a country code (such as 98765 43210), choose "No" and type the code to add, such as +91. Numbers that already start with + keep their own code.

### Tips

- Columns called Phone, Number or WhatsApp are matched to Mobile for you. Always check the mapping before importing.
- Excel files: only the first sheet is read, and its first row must hold the column names.
- Click "Verify numbers" to ask WhatsApp which numbers have an account. It runs slowly in the background through one of your phones. Then filter by WhatsApp status.
- Click "Export CSV" to save the list (or the current search) as a file.

### Be careful

- Only message people who agreed to hear from you. Messages to strangers get your number reported and banned.
- Getting the country code wrong sends messages to the wrong people. There is no default on purpose. Answer the question carefully.
- Opted-out numbers can still be imported, but RapBooster never messages them. Respect opt-outs: it is the law in many countries.

### Questions

#### Why were some rows "invalid"?

The number was missing, too short, or had no country code and you did not give one. An error report is saved to your exports folder so you can fix them.

#### Can I import an old .xls file?

No. Open it in Excel and save it as .xlsx or .csv, then import that file.

#### How does someone opt out?

By replying with exactly one of your opt-out words, such as STOP, in any letter case. Replying START lifts an opt-out they made themselves. You can also add or remove numbers by hand.

See also: [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Templates](#templates), [Sequences](#sequences), [WhatsApp Groups](#whatsapp-groups).

## Templates

A template is a message you write once and reuse in campaigns, sequences, group messages and auto-replies. It can be plain text, a photo or video with a caption, buttons, a list of options, a voice note, a sticker, a location, a contact card, a poll, an event invite or a product from your catalog. Merge tags such as `{{Name}}` fill in each person's details, and spintax varies the wording so every message is a little different.

Find it: click **Templates** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Create a text template

1. Click Templates in the sidebar, then "+ New Template".
2. Type a Template Name you will recognise later, such as "Diwali offer".
3. Keep the Template Type as "Text Only".
4. Write your message in "Message Content". Use `*stars*` for bold and `_underscores_` for italics, as in WhatsApp.
5. Check the Preview, then click "Create Template".

#### Personalise with merge tags

1. While writing, click a button under "Insert:", such as `{{Name}}`. It is added to the message.
2. Each person receives their own value. "Hi `{{Name}}`" becomes "Hi Priya".
3. The buttons come from the fields of your contact lists. Add custom fields when you create a list.
4. If the Preview warns "No list provides" a tag, that tag would send as a blank. Remove it or add the field to your list.

#### Vary the wording with spintax

1. Write choices inside curly brackets, separated by a straight line: `{Hi|Hello|Hey}`.
2. Each person gets one of the choices at random.
3. Check the count under the box. "3 variations" means it worked. "1 variation" means a typo in the brackets.
4. Click "Another variation" above the Preview to see other versions.

#### Add a photo, video or buttons

1. Choose "With Media (Image/Video)" as the Template Type.
2. Choose the Media Type, then click "Choose file…" and pick the file. It is copied into RapBooster.
3. Write a caption in "Message Content" if you want one.
4. For buttons, choose "Button Message", add up to 5 buttons and pick what each does: Quick reply, Open a link, Call a number or Copy a code.
5. Click "Create Template".

### Settings explained

- **Spintax**: Write `{Hi|Hello|Hey}` and each person gets one of the words at random, so not every message is identical. The count below shows how many different messages your text can make.
- **Merge tags**: A tag in double curly brackets, such as `{{Name}}`, is replaced with each person's own details when the message is sent. The buttons list the fields your contact lists have.

### Tips

- Button and list messages arrive as real WhatsApp buttons. If someone's WhatsApp cannot show them, they get a numbered list instead.
- A list ("Interactive Message") can have up to 10 options, one per line.
- Voice notes play best as OGG/Opus files. Stickers must be WebP files of 1 MB or less.
- To change a template, create a new one with your changes and use that from now on.

### Be careful

- Sending the exact same text to hundreds of people looks like spam to WhatsApp. Use spintax and merge tags so each message is different.

### Questions

#### Can I edit a template?

Not at the moment. Create a new template with the changes. You can delete the old one with the Delete button on its card, unless a campaign uses it.

#### Why can I not delete a template?

A template that a campaign uses cannot be deleted, so that campaign's history and any remaining messages stay correct. The message says how many campaigns use it.

#### What is the difference between `{Hi|Hello}` and `{{Name}}`?

One pair of curly brackets with straight lines is spintax: RapBooster picks one word. Two pairs of curly brackets is a merge tag: RapBooster fills in that person's details.

#### Which fields can I use as merge tags?

Name and Mobile always, plus any custom field you added to a contact list, such as Company or City.

See also: [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Sequences](#sequences), [Contacts](#contacts), [Automation](#automation).

## Campaigns

A campaign sends one template to everyone in the contact lists you choose, from one or more of your WhatsApp numbers. RapBooster sends the messages slowly, with random pauses, so your numbers look like a person and not a machine. You can pause, resume or stop a campaign at any time and see exactly who received it.

Find it: click **Campaigns** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Send your first campaign

1. Make a small test list on the Contacts screen first, with two or three of your own numbers.
2. Click Campaigns in the sidebar, then "+ Create Campaign".
3. Type a campaign name. Tick the phones to send from under "Select Devices".
4. Tick your test list under "Select Contact Lists", then choose a template under "Select Template".
5. Leave the four pacing boxes as they are unless you know you need something else.
6. Click "Create & Start". Watch the counters on the campaign card go up.
7. When the test looks right on your own phone, create the real campaign with your full list.

#### Schedule a campaign for later

1. Fill in the campaign as usual.
2. In "Schedule Send (optional)", pick the date and time.
3. The main button changes to Schedule. Click it.
4. The card shows the status Scheduled and the time it will start.

#### Pause, resume or stop a campaign

1. Find the campaign card on the Campaigns screen.
2. Click Pause to stop sending for now. Nothing is lost.
3. Click Resume to carry on from where it stopped.
4. Click Stop to finish it for good. People not yet reached will not get the message.
5. A draft campaign has a Start button instead.

#### See who received the message

1. On the campaign card, read Sent, Failed and Skipped, and Delivered, Read and Replied below them.
2. Click Recipients to see every person and their status. Use All, Sent, Failed, Pending and Skipped to filter.
3. The "Error / reason" column says why a message failed or was skipped.
4. Click Report to save the full list as a CSV file, which opens in Excel or Google Sheets. It opens when it is ready.

#### Target people by tag

1. Tag contacts on the Contacts screen first (for example "VIP").
2. In "Create Campaign", tick tags under "Include contacts tagged" to add those people.
3. Tick tags under "Exclude contacts tagged" to leave people out, even if they are in a chosen list.
4. Read the summary line at the bottom of the window. Each number is messaged only once.

### Settings explained

- **Random Delay From / To (sec)**: Before each message, RapBooster waits a random time between these two numbers of seconds. Random gaps look like a person typing. A few seconds or more is safer.
- **Sleep Duration / Sleep After N Messages**: After this many messages, the phone takes a longer break of this many seconds. Regular breaks make the sending pattern look natural.
- **Skip numbers not on WhatsApp**: Checks each number with WhatsApp just before sending. Numbers without WhatsApp are marked Skipped instead of Failed, which keeps your failure rate low.
- **Include / Exclude contacts tagged**: Include adds everyone with that tag, even if they are not in a chosen list. Exclude leaves people with that tag out, even if they are in a chosen list. Each number still gets one message.
- **Schedule Send (optional)**: Pick a date and time to start later. Leave it empty to start now. Quiet hours and daily limits still apply after it starts.

### Tips

- Tick "Skip numbers not on WhatsApp" to check each number just before sending. Numbers without WhatsApp are skipped instead of counted as failures.
- If the window warns that a merge tag such as `{{Company}}` is not in your lists, those messages would go out with a blank. Fix the template or the list first.
- Choosing several phones spreads the work. Each phone sends one message at a time.
- Duplicate copies a campaign's settings into a new draft. Use it to send the same message again later.

### Be careful

- Always test with a small list of your own numbers before sending to customers.
- Very short delays make a number look like a robot. Keep "Random Delay" at a few seconds or more, and keep the sleep pause.
- Each phone stops at its daily limit, and campaigns pause during quiet hours. The campaign carries on by itself when the limit resets or when quiet hours end.
- A duplicated campaign sends to everyone in its lists again, including people the first campaign already reached.
- People on your opt-out list are always skipped. Never remove someone from the opt-out list unless they asked you to.

### Questions

#### Why is my campaign running but nothing is being sent?

The usual reasons are: it is quiet hours, the phones reached their daily limit, a phone was paused for safety, or no chosen phone is connected. Check Devices and Settings › Sending & safety.

#### Can I change a campaign after it starts?

No. Pause it, stop it if needed, and create a new one. Use Duplicate to start from the same settings.

#### What does "Skipped" mean?

The person was not sent the message on purpose: they are on the opt-out list, or their number is not on WhatsApp. Skipped messages never count as failures.

#### How does RapBooster know someone replied because of my campaign?

A reply that arrives within the "Reply attribution window" after your message is counted as a reply to the campaign. You can change the window in Settings › Sending & safety.

See also: [Templates](#templates), [Contacts](#contacts), [Devices](#devices), [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety), [Sequences](#sequences).

## Inbox

The Inbox shows the WhatsApp conversations of every linked phone in one place. You can read and answer customers, send ready-made quick replies, schedule a message for later, approve replies written by the AI bot, and keep private notes about a customer.

Find it: click **Inbox** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Answer a customer

1. Click Inbox in the sidebar.
2. Pick a conversation from the list on the left. Use "Search chats..." or the device filter to find it.
3. Type your answer in the message box at the bottom.
4. Click Send. Your message goes out from the same WhatsApp number the customer wrote to.

#### Save and use quick replies

1. Click "Quick replies" at the top right of the Inbox.
2. Click "New quick reply". Give it a short shortcut (for example "prices"), a title and the message.
3. You can use `{{Name}}` in the message. It is replaced with the customer's name.
4. Click Save.
5. In any chat, type / in the message box. Pick a reply with the arrow keys and press Enter. Nothing is sent until you click Send.

#### Schedule a message for later

1. Open the chat and type the message, if you like.
2. Click Schedule next to Send.
3. Choose the date and time in "Send on". Check the message.
4. Optionally click "Choose file…" to add a photo, video or document.
5. Click Schedule. The waiting message shows above the message box, with a Cancel button.

#### Approve a reply written by the AI bot

1. Click the Drafts tab above the chat list to see chats with AI replies waiting.
2. Open a chat. The waiting reply shows at the top of the conversation.
3. Click Approve to send it as it is, or "Edit & approve" to change it first.
4. Click Discard if the reply is wrong. Nothing is sent.

#### See who you are talking to and add notes

1. Open a chat and click "Contact info" at the top right.
2. The panel shows the phone number, whether they opted out, their contact lists and tags.
3. It also shows which campaigns reached them (Sent, Delivered, Read, Replied) and their follow-up sequences.
4. Under Notes, type a note and click "Add note". Notes are private. The customer never sees them.

#### Take over a chat from the bot

1. Click the Escalated tab above the chat list.
2. These are chats the bot or a chatbot flow handed to a person. The bot stays quiet in them.
3. Answer the customer yourself.
4. When you are done, click "Resume bot" at the top of the chat to let the bot answer again.

### Tips

- Click the paperclip button to send a location, contact cards, a poll, a voice note or a sticker.
- Replies you type yourself are never held back by the daily limit or quiet hours. They still count toward the phone's total for today.
- Scheduled messages go out at the time you chose, even during quiet hours, but they count toward the daily limit. If RapBooster was closed at the time, they go out when you open it again.
- Photos, documents, voice notes, locations, polls and other special messages show as labelled cards in the conversation.

### Be careful

- A person shown as "Number hidden by WhatsApp" can still opt out: a STOP from them is honoured straight away. Their chat is never exported or added to a campaign, because there is no real number to send to.
- A chat marked "Opted out" asked not to receive messages. Campaigns, sequences and bots skip it. Only write to them if they contact you first and clearly want an answer.

### Questions

#### Why is the Inbox empty?

Conversations only appear for linked phones. Link a WhatsApp number on the Devices screen. New messages appear as they arrive.

#### Why does a chat say "Number hidden by WhatsApp"?

WhatsApp sometimes shares only a private ID instead of the phone number, especially in groups and for people you have not saved. You can still read and reply to the chat. As soon as WhatsApp reveals the number, RapBooster shows it everywhere by itself, and if you already had a chat with that number, the two chats are merged.

#### Can the customer see my notes?

No. Notes stay on this computer and are never sent to WhatsApp.

#### Why did my scheduled message not go out on time?

A scheduled message waits if the phone has reached its daily limit, and goes out when the limit resets. Quiet hours do not hold it back. A message to an opted-out number is never sent. The strip above the message box says why, with a Dismiss button.

See also: [AI Bot](#ai-bot), [Automation](#automation), [Contacts](#contacts), [Settings › Desktop](#settings--desktop).

## Sequences

A sequence is a series of follow-up messages sent over hours or days, one step at a time. For example: a welcome today, a reminder after two days and an offer after a week. Each person moves through the steps on their own clock, and the sequence can stop by itself as soon as they reply.

Find it: click **Sequences** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Create a sequence

1. Create the templates you need on the Templates screen first.
2. Click Sequences in the sidebar, then "+ New Sequence".
3. Type a name and tick the phones to send from under "Send From".
4. Leave "Stop when the contact replies" ticked unless you have a good reason.
5. For Step 1, choose a template and how long to wait after someone is enrolled.
6. Click "+ Add step" for each follow-up. Its wait counts from the previous step.
7. Click "Create Sequence".

#### Add people to a sequence

1. On the sequence card, click Enroll.
2. Tick one or more contact lists, or tags.
3. Click Enroll. Each number is added once.
4. People on the opt-out list and people already in this sequence are skipped.

#### See who is in a sequence

1. Read the counts on the card: Active, Completed, Stopped and Failed.
2. Click Enrollments to see each person and which step they are on.
3. Use the filters to show only Active, Completed, Stopped or Failed people.
4. Tick people and click "Unenroll selected" to take them out.

#### Pause, change or delete a sequence

1. Click Pause on the card to hold every step. Click Resume to carry on.
2. Click Edit to change the name, phones or steps, then Save.
3. Click Delete and confirm to remove the sequence.

### Settings explained

- **Wait (step delay)**: How long to wait before this step. Step 1 counts from when the person is enrolled; every other step counts from the previous step. Quiet hours and daily caps can make a step a little later.
- **Stop when the contact replies**: When the person writes back, they get no more steps from this sequence. Keep it on: following up after someone answered feels pushy.

### Tips

- A sequence can have up to 20 steps.
- Wait times can be in minutes, hours or days.
- Sequence messages follow the same pacing, daily limit and quiet hours as campaigns. A step due during quiet hours goes out when they end.
- Use a sequence for follow-ups and a campaign for one-off announcements.

### Be careful

- If you untick "Stop when the contact replies", people keep getting steps even after they answer you. That feels pushy and leads to blocks and reports.
- Someone who opts out, for example by sending STOP, gets no more steps from any sequence.

### Questions

#### When does the first message go out?

After the wait you set on Step 1, counted from the moment the person is enrolled. Set it to 0 minutes to send as soon as possible.

#### What happens if I pause a sequence for a week?

Nothing is sent while it is paused. When you resume, steps that became due are sent, paced as usual.

#### Why is someone "Stopped"?

They replied (when the sequence stops on reply), they opted out, their contact was deleted, or you unenrolled them. Hover over the row in Enrollments to see the reason.

See also: [Templates](#templates), [Contacts](#contacts), [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety).

## Status & Channels

Post WhatsApp Status updates and WhatsApp Channel messages from your linked numbers, now or at a time you choose. A Status is seen by your contacts for 24 hours. A Channel is a one-way feed that anyone can follow with its link.

Find it: click **Status & Channels** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Post a Status update

1. Click "Status & Channels" in the sidebar. The Status tab is open.
2. Choose the Device that should post it.
3. Choose the Type: Text, Image or Video.
4. Type the text, or choose the file and an optional caption. For text you can pick a background colour.
5. Under "Who can see it", keep "Every contact on file" or choose "Only these contact lists".
6. Choose "Post now", or "Schedule" and pick a date and time. Then click the button at the bottom.

#### Create or follow a Channel

1. Open the Channels tab.
2. Click "+ Create channel", choose a device, and type a channel name and description. Click Create.
3. To use a channel you already have, click "Follow channel" and paste its link (`https://whatsapp.com/channel/…`).
4. Click Copy next to a channel to copy its invite link and share it with customers.

#### Post to a Channel

1. Open the Channels tab.
2. In the post form, choose the device and a channel you own.
3. Choose the type, write the text or pick the file.
4. Choose "Post now" or "Schedule", then click the button at the bottom.

#### Check or cancel a scheduled post

1. Scroll down to "Status posts" or "Channel posts".
2. Each row shows where it goes, the device, the content, the time and its status.
3. Click Cancel on a post that has not gone out yet.
4. If a post failed, the Error column says why.

### Tips

- Image and video files are copied into RapBooster, so a scheduled post still works if you move the original file.
- Opted-out numbers never see your Status, even when you choose "Every contact on file".
- Scheduled posts go out at the time you chose, even during quiet hours.
- Removing a channel only forgets it in RapBooster. The channel itself stays on WhatsApp.

### Be careful

- You can only post to channels you own. A channel you follow can be read but not posted to.

### Questions

#### Who sees my Status?

The contacts you choose. WhatsApp usually only shows a Status to people who have your number saved in their phone, and it disappears after 24 hours.

#### My scheduled post did not go out. Why?

Posts go out while RapBooster is running and the chosen device is connected. A post that was due while the app was closed goes out soon after you open it. Check the Status and Error columns in the table.

See also: [Devices](#devices), [Contacts](#contacts), [WhatsApp Groups](#whatsapp-groups).

## WhatsApp Groups

WA Groups lists the WhatsApp groups and communities your linked phones belong to. You can send a template to several groups at once, create many groups in one go, join a group by its invite link, export group members into a contact list, and manage members, invite links and join requests in groups where you are an admin.

Find it: click **WA Groups** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Load your groups

1. Link at least one phone on the Devices screen.
2. Click WA Groups in the sidebar, then click Sync.
3. Your groups appear with their member count. "admin" means your number can manage the group.
4. Use "Filter by Device" to see the groups of one phone.

#### Send a message to several groups

1. Click each group you want, or "Select All".
2. Under "Send Messages to Groups", choose a template.
3. Set "Delay Between Messages (seconds)". A few seconds or more is safer.
4. Click "Send to Selected Groups".

#### Create many groups at once

1. Click "+ Create Bulk".
2. Choose the device, a "Group Name Prefix" (such as "Sales Team") and a "Suffix Rule" (001, 002… or A, B…).
3. Set how many groups to create and the delay between them.
4. Optionally tick contact lists and set "Contacts per Group" to add members.
5. Check the preview of the names, then click "Create Groups".

#### Manage a group where you are admin

1. Click Manage on the group's row.
2. On "Invite link", show, copy or reset the link.
3. On Settings, choose who can send messages and edit group info, and whether new members need approval.
4. On Members, add people by phone number or from a contact list, make someone admin, or remove them.
5. On "Join requests", approve or reject people waiting to join.

#### Save group members as a contact list

1. Select one or more groups.
2. Click "Export members".
3. Type a name for the new list and click Export.
4. The new list appears on the Contacts screen.

### Settings explained

- **Delay Between Messages (seconds)**: The wait between one group and the next. A few seconds or more looks natural and is safer for your number.

### Tips

- Click "Join via link" and paste a chat.whatsapp.com link to join a group with one of your phones.
- Open the Communities tab to create a community and link groups to it.
- WhatsApp privacy settings can stop some people being added to a group. Fewer members than you asked for is normal.
- Phone numbers for members must include the country code, such as +919876543210.

### Be careful

- Adding many strangers to groups is one of the fastest ways to get a number banned. Only add people who know you.
- Resetting an invite link stops the old link working for everyone who has it.
- Bulk group messages count toward each phone's daily limit and pause during quiet hours, like campaigns.

### Questions

#### Why can I not see the Members or Join requests of a group?

Only group admins can manage members and see join requests. Your number must be an admin of that group.

#### Why do some members show "Number hidden by WhatsApp"?

In groups, WhatsApp often shares only a private ID instead of a member's phone number. RapBooster replaces it with the real number as soon as WhatsApp reveals it. Until then that person is left out of exports and campaigns, because there is no real number to send to.

#### A group I just joined is missing. What do I do?

Click Sync again. Groups are read from your phones when you sync.

See also: [Devices](#devices), [Templates](#templates), [Contacts](#contacts), [Status & Channels](#status--channels).

## Automation

Automation answers customers for you, day and night. Chatbot flows guide people through menus and questions. Keyword rules send a fixed answer when a message contains a word such as "price". Welcome and away messages greet new customers and tell people when you are closed. Webhooks pass events to your other systems, and Calls can reject WhatsApp calls with a polite message.

Find it: click **Automation** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Answer a common question with a keyword rule

1. Click Automation in the sidebar. The "Keyword rules" tab is open.
2. Click "+ New rule" and give it a name, such as "Prices".
3. Type each keyword and press Enter after it, such as price, cost, rate.
4. Choose how the message must match, then write the reply text or choose a template.
5. Tick the phones the rule should answer on, then click "Save rule".
6. Type a sample message in "Test a message" and click Test to check which rule answers.

#### Build a chatbot menu

1. Open the "Chatbot flows" tab and click "+ New flow".
2. Pick a ready-made flow (Main menu, Lead capture or FAQ), or a blank one.
3. Click a step on the canvas and change its wording in the panel on the right.
4. Use "Add a step" to add a Message, Menu, Question, "Hand to a person" or End step.
5. Under "Start this flow", choose what starts it, such as a keyword like "menu".
6. Use "Test this flow" to chat with it. Nothing is sent to WhatsApp. Tick "Flow switched on" and click "Save flow".

#### Set up welcome and away messages

1. Open the "Welcome & away" tab.
2. Tick "Welcome message" and write the text. It goes once, to someone writing to you for the very first time.
3. Tick "Away message" and write the text.
4. Set your business hours for each day. Outside them, the away message is sent.
5. Choose how often the same chat can get the away message, then click Save.

#### Reject WhatsApp calls automatically

1. Open the Calls tab.
2. Tick "Automatically reject voice and video calls".
3. Write a short message for the caller, such as "We cannot take calls. Please send a message." Leave it empty to send nothing.
4. Click Save. Recent calls are listed below.

#### Send events to another system

1. Open the Webhooks tab and click "+ New webhook".
2. Paste the web address (URL) your other system gave you.
3. Tick the events to send, such as incoming messages or opt-outs, then click "Create webhook".
4. Copy the secret shown and give it to whoever runs the other system.
5. Click "Send test" to check it works, and Deliveries to see what was sent.

### Settings explained

- **Start this flow**: When the flow begins: when a message contains one of its keywords (whole words), on a new customer's first message, or on every message when no other flow is running.
- **Priority**: When two flows or two keyword rules could answer the same message, the higher number wins. Use it to make a specific answer beat a general one.
- **Match when the message…**: "Contains" finds the keyword anywhere as a whole word. "Starts with" needs it at the beginning. "Is exactly" needs the whole message to be just the keyword. Upper and lower case do not matter.
- **Cooldown per chat (minutes)**: After answering a chat, the rule stays quiet in that chat for this many minutes, so a customer who repeats a word does not get the same answer again and again.
- **Away message frequency**: The same chat gets the away message at most once in this many hours, even if the customer sends several messages at night.

### Tips

- Opt-out words are always handled first. Welcome and away messages go out alongside any other answer. After that come chatbot flows, then keyword rules, then the AI bot: the first of these that answers wins.
- A customer in the middle of a flow always gets the next step of that flow.
- In a flow, customers can answer a menu by typing the number, typing the choice's title, or tapping a button.
- Question steps save the answer. Later steps can use it, for example `{{name}}`.
- A flow waits 30 minutes for an answer. After that, the next message starts fresh.

### Be careful

- Automatic answers are never sent to groups, to chats that opted out or to numbers on your opt-out list.
- Automatic answers go out at any hour, quiet hours included, but they count toward each phone's daily limit. When the limit is reached they stop until it resets.
- Switching a flow off or deleting it ends the conversations that are in progress.

### Questions

#### Two rules match the same message. Which one answers?

The one with the higher Priority number. Flows work the same way: when two could start, the higher priority wins.

#### What does "Hand to a person" do?

It sends its message, marks the chat as Escalated in the Inbox, and stops the flow and the AI bot in that chat until you click "Resume bot".

#### Which time zone do business hours use?

The time zone of this computer.

See also: [AI Bot](#ai-bot), [Inbox](#inbox), [Templates](#templates), [Contacts](#contacts).

## AI Bot

The AI bot writes replies to your customers using an AI service such as OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude) or Google Gemini. You tell it about your business, your products and the questions people often ask, and it answers in the tone you choose. You can ask it to wait for your approval before anything is sent, and to hand a chat to a person when the customer is upset or asks for one.

Find it: click **AI Bot** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Connect an AI service

1. Create an account with the AI company you want to use and copy your API key from their website.
2. Click "AI Bot" in the sidebar.
3. Under "AI Provider", choose the Provider. Leave Model as it is unless you know which one you want.
4. Paste the key into the API key box and click "Save key".
5. Click "Test key". A green message means it works.

#### Teach the bot about your business

1. Under "System Instructions", describe how the bot should behave, such as "Be polite. Never promise discounts."
2. Fill in "Business Information": name, email and phone.
3. Under "Products & Services (Bulk)", write one product per line as: Name | Description.
4. Under "Knowledge Base (Bulk)", write one question per line as: Q: Question | A: Answer.
5. Click "Save Configuration".

#### Switch on automatic replies safely

1. Under "Limits & Safety", tick "Approve before sending" for the first days.
2. Set "Daily replies per device" and "Daily replies per chat" to sensible numbers.
3. Under "Auto-Reply Settings", tick "Enable Auto-Replies" and choose the Tone.
4. Click "Save Configuration".
5. Check the Drafts tab in the Inbox and approve, edit or discard each reply.
6. When you trust the answers, untick "Approve before sending" and save again.

#### Hand difficult chats to a person

1. Find "Escalation & Handling".
2. Choose an "Escalation Trigger", such as keywords like urgent, complaint or refund.
3. Optionally hand over after a number of bot replies, or after a conversation has run a number of minutes.
4. Write the "Escalation Message" the customer sees, such as "Connecting you with our team".
5. Click "Save Configuration". Escalated chats appear in the Inbox under Escalated.

### Settings explained

- **Provider and model**: The AI company that writes the replies, and which of its models to use. Each company has its own price per reply. Leave the model as it is unless you know you need another.
- **Response Delay**: A short pause before the bot answers, so the reply does not arrive unnaturally fast.
- **Approve before sending**: Bot replies wait in the Inbox (Drafts) until a person approves, edits or discards them. Use this while you learn how the bot answers.
- **Daily replies per device / per chat**: The most AI replies one phone, or one conversation, can get in a day. They protect you from a large bill and from a bot that talks too much. 0 means no limit.
- **Wait for more messages (sec)**: People often send several short messages in a row. The bot waits this long after the last one and answers them all in one reply.
- **History depth (messages)**: How many earlier messages of the chat the bot reads before answering. More history gives better answers but costs more.
- **Max tokens per reply**: The longest reply the bot may write. A token is roughly three quarters of a word. Smaller numbers give shorter, cheaper replies.
- **Temperature**: How creative the replies are. Low (such as 0.3) gives steady, predictable answers. High gives more varied answers that can wander off topic.
- **Escalation Trigger**: When the bot should stop and hand the chat to a person: when the customer uses words such as "complaint" or "refund", after a number of bot replies, or after a conversation has run a number of minutes.

### Tips

- The Usage panel shows how many replies and tokens were used today and this month. Tokens are what AI companies charge for.
- Lower "Temperature" gives more predictable answers. Higher gives more varied ones.
- "Wait for more messages" lets a customer finish typing. Several quick messages get one reply.
- Chatbot flows and keyword rules answer before the AI bot. Use them for questions with one fixed answer.

### Be careful

- The AI company charges you for every reply. Set daily limits so a busy day cannot run up a large bill.
- An AI can be confidently wrong. Start with "Approve before sending" switched on, and never let it promise prices or refunds you have not written down.
- Your API key is stored encrypted on this computer and only sent to the provider you chose. Never share it or paste it into a chat.

### Questions

#### Does the bot reply in groups?

No. It never replies in a group, never replies to itself and skips any chat that opted out. Its replies are paced like every other automated message.

#### Can I use a free model on my own computer?

Yes, if you run one that speaks the OpenAI format. Choose "OpenAI-compatible (local or gateway)" and type its Base URL, such as `http://localhost:11434/v1`.

#### Why did the bot not answer a customer?

Common reasons: auto-replies are switched off, a daily reply limit or the phone's daily limit was reached, the chat is escalated, the customer opted out, or a flow or keyword rule answered first. Quiet hours do not stop the bot. A reply held by the daily limit waits in the Inbox and goes out when the limit resets.

See also: [Automation](#automation), [Inbox](#inbox), [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety).

## Settings

Settings holds everything that applies to the whole app: your license, the safety limits every phone follows, how RapBooster looks and behaves on your computer, backups, and the diagnostics file our support team may ask for. Each part has its own section below.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Find a setting

1. Click Settings at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. Scroll to the section you need: License, "Data & diagnostics", Appearance, Desktop, "Sending & safety" or "Backup & restore".
3. A section with a Save button changes only when you click it. The Desktop and Appearance choices apply straight away.

#### Get help on one section

1. Click into the section you want to know about.
2. Press F1. The help panel opens on that section.
3. Hover over or focus a small "?" next to a setting to read what it does.

### Tips

- Most people only ever need "Sending & safety" and "Backup & restore".
- Your theme choice (Light, Dark or System) is also in the title bar at the top right.

### Be careful

- "Clear all data" removes every contact, template, campaign, group and message. Back up first.

### Questions

#### Where is my data stored?

On this computer. The "Data & diagnostics" section shows the exact folders. Your contacts and messages only leave this computer when you send them through WhatsApp, to your AI provider, or to a webhook you set up.

See also: [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety), [Settings › License](#settings--license), [Settings › Backup & restore](#settings--backup--restore), [Settings › Data & diagnostics](#settings--data--diagnostics), [Settings › Desktop](#settings--desktop), [Settings › Appearance](#settings--appearance).

## Settings › Sending & safety

These are the anti-ban rules every phone follows: how long to wait between messages, the most messages one phone may send in a day, the quiet hours when campaign-style sending pauses, and the warmup plan for new numbers. They protect your WhatsApp numbers from being restricted or banned.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Change the daily limit

1. Open Settings and scroll to "Sending & safety".
2. Change "Daily cap per device (0 = none)". The safe default is 200.
3. Click "Save sending defaults". The new limit applies to every phone at once, even mid-campaign.

#### Set quiet hours

1. In "Sending & safety", tick "Quiet hours".
2. Set From and Until, such as 21:00 until 09:00. The times are this computer's local time.
3. Click "Save sending defaults".
4. Campaigns, follow-up sequences, bulk group messages and warmup pause in this window (local time) and resume when it ends. Replies to customers — AI, chatbot flows, keyword and welcome/away replies — and messages you schedule still go out at any hour, within the daily limit.

#### Let your numbers chat with each other while warming up

1. Switch on Warmup for each new number on the Devices screen.
2. In Settings, under Warmup, tick "Warmup conversations between my devices".
3. Choose "Conversations per day".
4. Click "Save warmup". With two or more warmup numbers connected, they exchange a few short everyday messages.

### Settings explained

- **Daily cap per device**: The most automated messages one phone may send in a day: campaigns, sequences, group messages and automatic replies alike. When it is reached, they wait until it resets. Replies you type yourself are not limited. 200 is a safe start. 0 means no limit, which is risky.
- **Quiet hours**: Campaigns, follow-up sequences, bulk group messages and warmup pause in this window (local time) and resume when it ends. Replies to customers — AI, chatbot flows, keyword and welcome/away replies — and messages you schedule still go out at any hour, within the daily limit.
- **Retry attempts**: How many more times RapBooster tries a message that failed for a temporary reason, such as a weak connection, before marking it Failed.
- **Max devices sending at once**: How many of your phones may send at the same time. Each phone still sends only one message at a time.
- **Reply attribution window (hours)**: A reply that arrives within this many hours of a campaign message is counted as "Replied" for that campaign.
- **Group message delay / Group create delay**: The default wait between messages to groups, and between creating groups in bulk. Longer waits are safer.
- **Warmup conversations between my devices**: With two or more warmup numbers connected, they send each other a few short everyday messages, spread over the day and outside quiet hours. These count toward each phone's daily cap.

### Tips

- The four delay boxes here are the starting values for new campaigns. A running campaign keeps its own delays.
- Leave "Health breaker" on. It pauses a phone automatically when its messages start failing like a ban is coming.
- "Simulate typing" shows "typing…" before each automated message, like a person would.

### Be careful

- Setting the daily cap to 0 removes the limit. WhatsApp bans numbers that send hundreds of messages a day, especially new ones.
- Turning quiet hours off means campaigns and sequences can message people in the middle of the night. That leads to blocks and reports.
- Very short delays are risky. Keep a random delay of a few seconds and a sleep pause after every few messages.

### Questions

#### What are the safe defaults?

A daily cap of 200 messages per phone and quiet hours from 21:00 to 09:00, both switched on for a new installation. New numbers should use Warmup on top of that.

#### Does warmup chat count toward the daily limit?

Yes. Warmup conversations count toward each phone's daily limit.

See also: [Devices](#devices), [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Settings](#settings).

## Settings › License

The License section shows whether your license is valid, which computer it is bound to, and when it expires. You can re-check it now, or release it from this computer so you can use it on another one.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Move your license to another computer

1. On the old computer, open Settings and find License.
2. Click "Deactivate this device", then Confirm.
3. On the new computer, install RapBooster and enter the same license key.

#### Re-check your license

1. Make sure the computer is online.
2. Click "Re-check now".
3. The Status updates. "valid" means everything is fine.

### Tips

- If the computer is offline, RapBooster keeps working for a grace period. "Offline grace until" shows how long.

### Be careful

- Deactivating takes this computer back to the activation screen. Keep your license key: you need it to use RapBooster here again.

### Questions

#### My license says "conflict". What does that mean?

The key is already active on another computer. Deactivate it there first, or contact your seller.

See also: [Settings](#settings), [Settings › Data & diagnostics](#settings--data--diagnostics).

## Settings › Data & diagnostics

This section shows where RapBooster keeps its database and log files, and which version you are running. "Export diagnostics" makes one file our support team can read to find a problem. It never contains your message text, and phone numbers and keys in it are hidden.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Send diagnostics to support

1. Open Settings and find "Data & diagnostics".
2. Click "Export diagnostics".
3. The folder with the new file opens.
4. Attach that file to your email or message to support, and say what you were doing when the problem happened.

### Tips

- "Open logs folder" shows the log files, if support asks for them directly.

### Questions

#### Is it safe to send the diagnostics file?

Yes. It contains no message content, and phone numbers, license keys and API keys are hidden before the file is written.

See also: [Settings](#settings), [Help Center](#help-center).

## Settings › Appearance

Choose Light, Dark or System. System follows your Windows or macOS setting by itself. A phone preview shows how your messages look to customers, including WhatsApp formatting.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Switch to dark mode

1. Open Settings and find Appearance.
2. Click Dark. The whole app changes at once.
3. Choose System to follow your computer instead.

### Tips

- WhatsApp formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~` and ` ```monospace``` `.
- The same Light, Dark and System buttons are in the title bar.

See also: [Settings](#settings).

## Settings › Desktop

Choose how RapBooster behaves on your computer: desktop notifications for new messages, whether it keeps running in the tray when you close the window, and whether it starts when the computer starts.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Keep campaigns sending after closing the window

1. Open Settings and find Desktop.
2. Switch on "Keep running when the window is closed".
3. Closing the window now leaves RapBooster in the tray (the menu bar on a Mac).
4. To stop everything, choose Quit from the tray icon.

#### Get notified about new messages

1. Switch on "Notify me about new messages".
2. When a customer writes and RapBooster is not in front, a notification appears.
3. Click it to open that chat.

### Tips

- "Start RapBooster when the computer starts" opens it quietly in the tray, so campaigns and replies carry on after a restart. It works on Windows and macOS.
- On a Mac, closing the window never quits. Use Quit (⌘Q) or the tray menu.
- You get at most one notification per chat every 10 seconds.

### Be careful

- If RapBooster is not running, nothing is sent: campaigns, sequences, scheduled messages and auto-replies all wait.

See also: [Settings](#settings), [Inbox](#inbox).

## Settings › Backup & restore

A backup is a copy of everything in RapBooster: contacts, templates, campaigns and message history. RapBooster makes one by itself before every update to its database and before clearing data. You can also make one whenever you like.

Find it: click **Settings** in the sidebar, then scroll to this section.

### Things you can do

#### Make a backup

1. Open Settings and find "Backup & restore".
2. Click "Back up now".
3. The folder with the backup opens. Copy the file to a USB drive or cloud storage for safe keeping.

#### Start again with no data

1. Make a backup first.
2. Under "Clear all data", type DELETE in the box.
3. Click "Clear all data". Devices and your license are kept.

### Tips

- Click "Open backups folder" to see every backup RapBooster has made.

### Be careful

- Clearing data cannot be undone except from a backup.
- Backups stay on this computer. If the computer is lost, so are they. Keep a copy somewhere else.

### Questions

#### How do I restore a backup?

There is no restore button on this screen. Keep the backup file safe and contact support: they will guide you through restoring it, so nothing current is lost by mistake.

See also: [Settings](#settings), [Settings › Data & diagnostics](#settings--data--diagnostics).

## Help Center

The Help Center collects all of RapBooster's help in one place: a guide to every screen, the safety rules that protect your WhatsApp numbers, answers to common problems, a dictionary of the words the app uses, and the keyboard shortcuts. You can also restart any guided tour, bring back the getting-started checklist, and find out how to contact support.

Find it: click **Help Center** in the sidebar.

### Things you can do

#### Search the help

1. Type a few words in the search box, such as "daily limit" or "QR code".
2. Click a result to read it.
3. You can also press F1 on any screen to open help for that screen, with the same search.

#### Take a guided tour again

1. In the Help Center, find "Guided tours".
2. Click the screen you want to learn about.
3. RapBooster opens that screen and points at each part in turn. Use Next and Back, or the arrow keys.
4. Press Escape or click Skip to stop at any time.

#### Contact support

1. Write down what you were doing and what you expected to happen.
2. Click "Export diagnostics" in the "Contact support" section, or in Settings under "Data & diagnostics".
3. Send the file together with your description to your RapBooster seller or support contact.

### Tips

- Every screen has a "?" button next to its title. It opens the help for that screen.
- Small "?" icons next to settings explain them. Hover over them or reach them with the Tab key.

See also: [Dashboard](#dashboard), [Settings › Data & diagnostics](#settings--data--diagnostics).

## Troubleshooting

### My phone will not connect

The phone is offline, WhatsApp removed the link, or the connection dropped and is waiting to retry.

1. Check that the phone is switched on and has internet. Open WhatsApp on it once.
2. On the Devices screen, click Reconnect on the card and wait up to a minute.
3. If the card says "Logged out", the link was removed on the phone. Click "+ Add Device" and link it again.
4. If a red message shows on the card, read it: it says what went wrong.
5. Still stuck? Restart RapBooster, then export diagnostics and contact support.

See also: [Devices](#devices).

### The QR code expired or will not scan

WhatsApp changes the QR code every 20 seconds or so, and stops after a few tries if nobody scans it.

1. Close the "Add WhatsApp Device" window.
2. Click "+ Add Device" again and click "Generate QR & Connect". Have your phone ready first.
3. On the phone, go to WhatsApp, then Settings, then "Linked Devices", then "Link a Device", and scan straight away.
4. Hold the phone steady about 20 cm from the screen. Make the window larger if the code is small.
5. If scanning keeps failing, use the "Pairing code" tab instead.

See also: [Devices](#devices).

### My campaign is running but nothing is being sent

RapBooster is holding messages back on purpose to protect your numbers, or no phone can send right now.

1. Quiet hours: check the time. Campaigns pause during quiet hours and carry on when they end (Settings › Sending & safety).
2. Daily cap: open Devices. A full usage bar means the phone reached its limit. Sending carries on tomorrow.
3. Warmup: a number in warmup has a lower limit for its first ten days.
4. Safety pause: a card that says "Paused for safety" stopped because of failures. Read why before clicking "Resume now".
5. Connection: the campaign needs at least one of its chosen phones to be Connected.

See also: [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Devices](#devices), [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety).

### Some people were skipped

Skipped messages were left out on purpose, never by mistake.

1. Open the campaign's Recipients and choose Skipped.
2. Read the "Error / reason" column.
3. "Opted out" means the person asked not to be messaged. Respect it.
4. A number not on WhatsApp cannot receive messages. Use "Verify numbers" on the Contacts screen to clean your lists.

See also: [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Contacts](#contacts).

### Many messages failed

Usually wrong numbers, numbers not on WhatsApp, a lost connection, or WhatsApp limiting your number.

1. Pause the campaign.
2. Open Recipients, choose Failed, and read the reasons.
3. Wrong or short numbers: check the country code in your list and import again.
4. Not on WhatsApp: tick "Skip numbers not on WhatsApp" in your next campaign.
5. If failures started suddenly on one phone, read "My account got a warning" below before sending more.

See also: [Campaigns](#campaigns), [Contacts](#contacts), [Devices](#devices).

### My account got a warning, or I am worried about a ban

WhatsApp restricts numbers that send too many messages, send too fast, or get blocked and reported by people who did not expect them.

1. Stop or pause every campaign on that number at once.
2. Do not log out and link again over and over. Let the number rest for a few days.
3. Lower the daily cap in Settings › Sending & safety, and switch on Warmup for that number.
4. Only message people who agreed to hear from you, and honour every opt-out.
5. Use spintax and merge tags so messages are not identical, and keep the random delays.

See also: [Settings › Sending & safety](#settings--sending--safety), [Devices](#devices), [Templates](#templates).

### A contact shows "Number hidden by WhatsApp"

WhatsApp sometimes shares only a private ID instead of the phone number, especially in groups and for people who are not saved in your phone.

1. You can still read and reply to their chat in the Inbox as usual.
2. Wait: as soon as WhatsApp reveals the number, RapBooster replaces it everywhere by itself.
3. If you already had a chat with that number, the two chats are merged into one.
4. A STOP from this person is honoured straight away, like any other opt-out.
5. Hidden numbers are never exported or added to campaigns, because there is no real number to send to.

See also: [Inbox](#inbox), [WhatsApp Groups](#whatsapp-groups).

### The AI bot does not answer or says the key is wrong

The key was mistyped, has no credit left, belongs to another provider, or a reply limit was reached.

1. Open AI Bot and check the Provider matches the company your key came from.
2. Paste the key again, click "Save key", then "Test key".
3. If the test fails, log in to the AI company's website and check that your account has credit.
4. Check "Enable Auto-Replies" is ticked and the daily reply limits are not used up (see the Usage panel).
5. Check the chat is not escalated, opted out or a group. The bot never answers those.

See also: [AI Bot](#ai-bot).

### My contacts will not import

The file type is not supported, or the columns or numbers are not in the expected shape.

1. Use a .csv, .xlsx or .vcf file. Save old .xls files as .xlsx first.
2. Make sure the first row has column names, such as Name and Phone.
3. Map one column to Mobile.
4. Answer the country code question. Numbers without a country code are reported as invalid.
5. Open the error report in your exports folder to see which rows failed and why.

See also: [Contacts](#contacts).

### Nothing was sent while my computer was off

RapBooster sends from this computer. When it is closed or the computer is asleep, everything waits.

1. Keep RapBooster running while campaigns run. Closing the window can leave it running in the tray (Settings › Desktop).
2. Switch on "Start RapBooster when the computer starts" so it carries on after a restart.
3. When you open it again, waiting campaigns, sequences and scheduled messages carry on by themselves.

See also: [Settings › Desktop](#settings--desktop).

### How do I send diagnostics to support?

A diagnostics file lets support see what happened without seeing your messages.

1. Open Settings and find "Data & diagnostics", or open Help Center and find "Contact support".
2. Click "Export diagnostics". The folder with the file opens.
3. Send that file to support with a short description of the problem and when it happened.
4. The file has no message content, and phone numbers and keys are hidden.

See also: [Settings › Data & diagnostics](#settings--data--diagnostics), [Help Center](#help-center).

## Glossary

- **AI bot**: An automatic helper that writes replies to customers using an AI service such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Set it up on the AI Bot screen.
- **API key**: A long secret code from an AI company that lets RapBooster use your account with them. Treat it like a password.
- **Campaign**: One message (a template) sent to many people from your contact lists, paced slowly by RapBooster to keep your numbers safe.
- **Channel**: A WhatsApp Channel: a one-way feed of updates that anyone can follow with its link. Followers cannot reply.
- **Contact list**: A named group of people with their phone numbers, such as "Customers" or "Leads". Campaigns and sequences send to lists.
- **Country code**: The digits in front of a phone number that say which country it is in, such as +91 for India or +44 for the United Kingdom. WhatsApp needs it.
- **Daily cap**: The most automated messages one phone may send in a day. When it is reached, sending waits until the next day. The safe default is 200.
- **Device**: One WhatsApp number linked to RapBooster, like WhatsApp Web. You can link up to 20.
- **Draft (AI draft)**: A reply the AI bot wrote that is waiting for a person to approve, edit or discard it in the Inbox.
- **Escalated chat**: A conversation the bot or a flow handed to a person. The bot stays quiet there until you click "Resume bot".
- **Flow (chatbot flow)**: A set of automatic steps, such as a menu and questions, that guides a customer to an answer or to a person. Built on the Automation screen.
- **Health breaker**: A safety switch that pauses a phone by itself when its messages start failing at an unusual rate, which can be a sign of a coming ban.
- **Hidden number**: Shown as "Number hidden by WhatsApp" when WhatsApp shares only a private ID instead of a phone number. RapBooster fills in the real number as soon as WhatsApp reveals it.
- **Keyword rule**: An automatic answer sent when a customer's message contains a word you chose, such as "price".
- **Merge tag**: A word in double curly brackets, such as `{{Name}}`, that is replaced with each person's own details when the message is sent.
- **Opt-out**: A person who asked not to receive messages, for example by replying STOP. RapBooster never sends them campaigns, sequences or automatic replies.
- **Pacing**: The random waits and regular breaks between messages that make sending look like a person instead of a machine.
- **Pairing code**: An 8-character code you type on your phone to link it to RapBooster, instead of scanning a QR code.
- **QR code**: The square barcode RapBooster shows when you link a phone. You scan it from WhatsApp, under Linked Devices.
- **Quick reply**: A saved answer you insert in the Inbox by typing / and picking it, such as your price list or opening hours.
- **Quiet hours**: A time window, such as 21:00 to 09:00, when campaigns, follow-up sequences, bulk group messages and warmup pause. Replies to customers and messages you schedule still go out.
- **Sequence**: A series of follow-up messages sent one step at a time over hours or days, which can stop when the person replies.
- **Spintax**: Choices written as `{Hi|Hello|Hey}`. Each person gets one of them at random, so not every message is the same.
- **Status**: A WhatsApp Status update: text, a photo or a video your contacts can see for 24 hours.
- **Tag**: A label such as "VIP" you put on contacts, to target or leave them out of campaigns and sequences.
- **Template**: A message you write once and reuse in campaigns, sequences, groups and auto-replies.
- **Token**: The unit AI companies charge by. A token is roughly three quarters of a word.
- **Warmup**: A plan for new numbers: the daily limit starts at 20 messages and grows over ten days, so WhatsApp sees normal, gradual use.
- **Webhook**: A way to tell another computer system, such as a CRM, when something happens in RapBooster, for example a new message or an opt-out.
- **Welcome and away messages**: Automatic greetings: a welcome for someone writing to you for the first time, and an away message outside your business hours.

## Frequently asked questions

Questions about a single screen are answered in that screen's chapter, under "Questions".

### Is RapBooster an official WhatsApp product?

No. It links to your WhatsApp numbers the same way WhatsApp Web does. You are responsible for following WhatsApp's rules and the law where you live.

### Does RapBooster need to stay open?

Yes, to send. Messages go out from this computer. You can close the window and keep it running in the tray (Settings › Desktop).

### What do quiet hours stop, and what still goes out?

Quiet hours pause campaigns, follow-up sequences, bulk group messages and warmup. Replies to customers (AI bot, chatbot flows, keyword replies, welcome and away messages, call auto-reply and opt-out confirmations) and messages you scheduled for a set time (inbox messages, Status and Channel posts) still go out at any hour. Everything automated still counts toward the daily limit; replies you type yourself in the Inbox ignore both.

### How many WhatsApp numbers can I use?

Up to 20 at the same time. Each one sends one message at a time.

### Can I use WhatsApp on my phone at the same time?

Yes. Linking RapBooster works like WhatsApp Web, so your phone keeps working as normal.

### Where do I start?

Follow the getting-started checklist on the Dashboard: link your number, import contacts, create a template, then send a small test campaign.

### How do I get help on the screen I am looking at?

Press F1, or click the "?" next to the screen's title. To learn a screen step by step, choose "Take the tour".

## Keyboard shortcuts

- `F1`: Open help for the screen you are on. Press again to close it.
- `Escape`: Close the help panel, a window or a tooltip, or stop a guided tour.
- `→ or Enter`: During a guided tour: go to the next step.
- `←`: During a guided tour: go back one step.
- `/`: In the Inbox message box: pick a quick reply. Use ↑ and ↓ to choose and Enter to insert.
- `Enter`: In the Inbox message box: send the message.
- `Enter`: In a keyword box (keyword rules and chatbot flows): add the keyword you typed.
- `Tab / Shift+Tab`: Move between buttons and boxes without the mouse.
- `← and →`: Move between tabs, or between the Light, Dark and System theme choices.
- `⌘Q`: On a Mac: quit RapBooster completely. On Windows, right-click the tray icon and choose Quit.
